headline: Trump Awards Top Science Prizes to Tech CEOs Amidst Donations
summary: Elon Musk, Jensen Huang, Sergey Brin, and Lisa Su received the National Medal of Science, while Michael Dell and Satya Nadella were honored with the National Medal of Technology and Innovation.
details: President Trump presented the National Medal of Science to tech leaders including Elon Musk, Jensen Huang, Sergey Brin, and AMD CEO Lisa Su at the Golden Age of American Innovation Summit.
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella and Dell Technologies founder Michael Dell were awarded the National Medal of Technology and Innovation.
These honorees and their companies have collectively donated nearly $6 billion to Trump-affiliated campaigns and initiatives, according to The New Republic.
Trump stated that the recipients have "pioneered an incredible future for America," ensuring the nation's continued global leadership.
The awards come shortly after Microsoft's indefinite suspension from the H-1B visa program, which allows U.S. companies to hire skilled foreign workers.
caption:
Tech titans like Elon Musk and Jensen Huang received top science awards from President Trump, following significant donations to his administration.

President Trump presented the National Medal of Science to tech leaders including Elon Musk, Jensen Huang, Sergey Brin, and AMD CEO Lisa Su at the Golden Age of American Innovation Summit.

Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella and Dell Technologies founder Michael Dell were awarded the National Medal of Technology and Innovation.

These honorees and their companies have collectively donated nearly $6 billion to Trump-affiliated campaigns and initiatives, according to The New Republic.

Trump stated that the recipients have "pioneered an incredible future for America," ensuring the nation's continued global leadership.

The awards come shortly after Microsoft's indefinite suspension from the H-1B visa program, which allows U.S. companies to hire skilled foreign workers.

headline: SpaceX plans to become a major US mobile carrier with Starlink Mobile
summary: The company acquired low-band spectrum licenses to directly compete with T-Mobile, AT&T, and Verizon, aiming for seamless indoor and outdoor coverage.
details: SpaceX has announced its intention to become a major US mobile carrier by acquiring a portfolio of low-band spectrum licenses. This strategic move, pending FCC approval, will enable its Starlink Mobile service to directly challenge established giants like T-Mobile, AT&T, and Verizon.

The acquired licenses include up to 14 megahertz of paired spectrum in the 800 MHz band. SpaceX states this will allow Starlink Mobile's signal to penetrate walls and buildings, ensuring more reliable connectivity.

This acquisition follows SpaceX's previous purchase of 2GHz spectrum from EchoStar, further bolstering its direct-to-device service capabilities. The company is also set to deploy 15,000 V2 Starlink Mobile satellites, promising over 100 times the bandwidth of the current generation.

SpaceX aims to create a unified network that offers reliable service everywhere, including cellular dead zones and indoors. This integrated approach combines satellite and terrestrial spectrum, positioning Starlink Mobile as a comprehensive connectivity solution for Americans.
caption:
